achievements:title: Achievements
achievements:progress__note: Overall count. Both are whole numbers.
achievements:group.earned__note: Section heading over achievements with at least one tier unlocked. Max 16 characters.
achievements:group.close__note: Section heading over the unearned achievements nearest their first tier. Short and unpressured — not "Almost there!", which is a nudge rather than a label. Max 16 characters.
achievements:group.rest__note: Section heading over the remaining unearned achievements. Deliberately neutral — not "Locked", which this screen never says. Max 20 characters.
achievements:locked__note: Shown instead of a tier on an achievement with no tier earned. Max 12 characters.
achievements:next__note: How much is left before the next tier. {remaining} is a whole number.
achievements:empty.action__note: Button on the empty achievements state. The next step that actually fixes it.
achievements:empty.title: Nothing unlocked yet
achievements:empty.body: Finish a lesson and the first one is already within reach.

achievements:facts.everything.name__note: Achievement name. Playful, never smug — it is the reward for finishing the whole app, not a label for the person. Max 16 characters.
achievements:codes.collector.name__note: Achievement name for learning international dialling codes. A pun on a phone tone; if it does not translate, name it plainly. Max 16 characters.
achievements:languages.collector.desc__n: The number is 26 rather than 65 because only 26 countries in the pack carry a language fact. Never round it up — an unreachable target with a progress bar is the dark pattern the content rules forbid.
achievements:currencies.collector.name__: Achievement name for learning currencies. A person who changes money, not a coin — the achievements are titles you wear. Max 16 characters.
achievements:locations.collector.name__n: Achievement name for learning where countries are on the map. Max 16 characters.
achievements:languages.collector.name__n: Achievement name for learning which language a country speaks. "Polyglot" is the standard word in most European languages; use the local equivalent rather than translating it literally. Max 16 characters.
